content.title: Is WrestleMania 42 on Netflix? How to watch live
content.text: WWE WrestleMania 42 is the biggest professional wrestling event of the year, taking place over two spectacular nights at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. Night 1 is Saturday, April 18, and Night 2 is Sunday, April 19, 2026, with both nights kicking off at 6:00 PM ET / 3:00 PM PT. The card features some of the most anticipated matches in recent memory, including CM Punk vs Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship and Cody Rhodes defending the Undisputed WWE Championship against Randy Orton. Streaming availability for WrestleMania 42 varies by country – Netflix carries it live in most international territories, while US viewers need an ESPN Unlimited subscription. If you're traveling abroad and your usual streaming service doesn't show the event, a VPN can help you access your home library from anywhere. Does WrestleMania 42 stream on Netflix?In the United States, WrestleMania 42 is not on Netflix. Both nights stream exclusively through the ESPN App, which requires an active ESPN Unlimited subscription at $29.99/month. This applies whether you watch through the app, browser, or a TV provider that includes ESPN Unlimited. Outside the US, Netflix is the home of WrestleMania 42. Confirmed Netflix territories include the UK, Ireland, Australia, Canada, Brazil, Argentina, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Chile, Colombia, and many more regions across Europe, Latin America, and Asia-Pacific. If you're in one of these territories, WrestleMania 42 will appear automatically in your Netflix library. However, if you're traveling abroad and your current location doesn't show the event in your Netflix catalog, you can use a VPN to connect back to a supported region and access your home library. WrestleMania 42 match card previewWrestleMania 42 features eight championship matches across two nights, making it one of the most title-rich cards in the event's history. Night 1–Saturday, April 18The headline match of Night 1 sees Cody Rhodes defend the Undisputed WWE Championship against Randy Orton, with Pat McAfee in Orton's corner. Rhodes has been champion since WrestleMania 40, and Orton's return to the WrestleMania main event picture makes this one of the most emotionally charged matches on the card. AJ Lee defends the Women's Intercontinental Championship against Becky Lynch in what promises to be a technically sharp bout between two of the most decorated performers in the women's division. The Women's World Championship is also on the line as Stephanie Vaquer defends against Liv Morgan. Seth Rollins takes on GUNTHER in a match that has been building for months, while a Women's Tag Team Championship Fatal 4-Way features Nia Jax & Lash Legend defending against Charlotte Flair & Alexa Bliss, Bayley & Lyra Valkyria, and The Bella Twins. The opening ESPN hour on Night 1 includes Jacob Fatu vs. Drew McIntyre and the six-man tag of Logan Paul, Austin Theory & IShowSpeed vs. LA Knight, Jey Uso & Jimmy Uso. Night 2–Sunday, April 19The main event of Night 2 is the long-awaited CM Punk vs. Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship – a match that has been over a year in the making and carries enormous personal stakes for both men. Jade Cargill faces Rhea Ripley for the WWE Women's Championship, and Sami Zayn defends the United States Championship against Trick Williams in what is expected to be a crowd-pleasing contest. The ESPN opening hour on Night 2 features Brock Lesnar vs. Oba Femi – a match reportedly pushed by ESPN to include a marquee name in the broadcast window – as well as the Intercontinental Championship Ladder Match with Penta defending against Je'Von Evans and additional participants. Final thoughtsWrestleMania 42 is a two-night event with something for every fan, and how you watch it comes down entirely to where you are in the world.
